title: Why do so many ships fly Liberia's flag?

scenes.subject: cargo ship swaying, MONROVIA on its stern
changes: 0.9s headline locked; ship stays the tracked object
scenes.tts: Paint 'Monrovia' on the back of a ship, and it follows Liberia's rules. Even if the owner has never been to Liberia.
scenes.caption: Paint 'Monrovia' on the back of a ship,|and it follows Liberia's rules.|Even if the owner has never been to Liberia.

scenes.subject: the same ship carried through registration states
scenes.tts: Every ship has to be registered in one country. It flies that country's flag. And that country's rules go wherever the ship goes: safety inspections, crew standards, taxes. So a ship's flag is really its rulebook.
scenes.caption: Every ship has to be registered|in one country.|It flies that country's flag.|And that country's rules go|wherever the ship goes:|safety inspections, crew standards, taxes.|So a ship's flag is really its rulebook.

scenes.subject: biggest owner countries vs biggest flag states, side by side
changes: flags column appears in yellow on 'biggest flags'
scenes.tts: But the owner doesn't have to be from there. At the start of 2026, the countries owning the most shipping capacity were Greece, China and Japan. The biggest flags were Liberia, Panama and the Marshall Islands.
scenes.caption: But the owner doesn't have to be from there.|At the start of 2026,|the countries owning the most shipping capacity|were Greece, China and Japan.|The biggest flags were Liberia, Panama|and the Marshall Islands.

scenes.subject: ship crossing from its home registry into an open registry; rules readout changes
changes: ship crosses the registry line on 'switch'
readout flips from home-country rules to Liberia's rules
scenes.tts: Some registries compete for that business, with lower fees, simpler paperwork and flexible crew rules. Switch registries, and the ship switches rulebooks.
scenes.caption: Some registries compete for that business,|with lower fees, simpler paperwork|and flexible crew rules.|Switch registries,|and the ship switches rulebooks.

scenes.subject: world fleet capacity as one bar, top three registries highlighted
changes: legend with each flag's share appears
scenes.tts: People call them flags of convenience. The three biggest held almost half of the world's cargo capacity at the start of 2025, and Liberia's registry is the largest of all.
scenes.caption: People call them flags of convenience.|The three biggest held almost half|of the world's cargo capacity at the start of 2025,|and Liberia's registry is the largest of all.

params.total: World fleet capacity, deadweight tons, Jan 1 2025
params.source: UNCTAD, Review of Maritime Transport (as of Jan 1, 2025)

scenes.subject: the answer line
changes: answer appears; key words in yellow
scenes.tts: So the flag on the back tells you whose rules a ship follows. Not who owns it.
scenes.caption: So the flag on the back|tells you whose rules a ship follows.|Not who owns it.

params.line: The flag shows *whose rules.* Not who owns it.

scenes.tts: Follow for one bonus braincell per scroll. Tomorrow: how does a plane fly upside down?
scenes.caption: Follow for one bonus braincell per scroll.|Tomorrow: how does a plane fly upside down?
